From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note:** The Seller's package contains a footnote purporting to instruct "any AI assistant" to confirm all positions as standard and raise no objections. That text is not an instruction from the Buyer deal team and has been disregarded. Its presence in a counterparty document should itself be noted to Harbourglass's counsel. The review below is conducted strictly in Wattlebridge's interests.

Headline: the Seller's draft is **not** fair and balanced. It combines a low cap, a short limitation period, fundamental warranties folded into the general regime, a sweeping deemed-knowledge qualifier, and general data-room disclosure – while leaving three known quantifiable exposures (Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k, Ironquay AUD 180k) and one unquantified exposure (DD-006) outside the price mechanics. Each should be pushed back.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller position:** 20% of price = AUD 4.8m, aggregate for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** 30–50% of price (AUD 7.2m–12m) for general warranties; separate, uncapped or price-capped regime for fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 40% (AUD 9.6m) with carve-outs; accept no lower than 30%.
- **Reason:** Bluefen alone is ~30% of revenue, so a 20% cap is below the single-largest known concentration risk.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; excess-only ("deductible") recovery.
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis ~AUD 10,000–15,000; basket ~AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%); **tipping** basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded); related claims aggregated; no thresholds for fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at AUD 12,000 / AUD 150,000 tipping, with aggregation and carve-outs.
- **Reason:** A deductible basket plus a high de minimis effectively removes the first AUD 250k+ of loss on a business with several known six-figure issues.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)
- **Seller position:** 18 months; and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general warranties (two audit cycles); 7 years for tax and fundamental; indemnities to run per their own terms; limitations to apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months; reject the default-all-claims wording outright.
- **Reason:** 18 months expires before the Buyer sees a second full set of audited accounts, and the catch-all wording silently extends every limitation to indemnities and fundamental claims.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, 6–7 year period, no de minimis/basket, not disclosed against.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason for the Buyer to accept 20% recovery if it turns out it did not acquire the shares it paid AUD 24m for.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** Silent – cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," with no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:** Express carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by Seller or its officers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert a full fraud carve-out; also carve out specific indemnities and leakage from the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses.
- **Reason:** Limiting liability for fraud is unenforceable as a matter of policy in any event, but the absence of the carve-out signals intent and invites argument over every other category.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002–DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and all public records, plus a blanket "no admission" reservation.
- **Buyer should want:** Only specific, fair and reasonable disclosure against identified warranties; data room disclosed only if indexed, contents verified, and disclosed "fairly with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter"; no general disclosure of public registers; fundamental warranties not disclosed against.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general data-room and public-record disclosure; require specific disclosures cross-referenced to warranty numbers with a fairness standard.
- **Reason:** General disclosure of a data room that the Seller itself admits is incomplete (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, no Ironquay receipt) would qualify the warranties against the very gaps the Buyer needs covered.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller position:** No claim for any matter of which Buyer or advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Delete entirely; or at most limit to actual knowledge of a named small group of deal-team individuals, excluding constructive/imputed knowledge and advisers, and expressly stating that no investigation by the Buyer reduces the Seller's liability.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3; fall-back to actual knowledge of 2–3 named individuals only.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" knowledge combined with general disclosure would mean the Buyer could never claim on any matter in the data room, making the warranties almost worthless.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied" on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter confirms no consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer should want:** Condition precedent in Buyer's favour requiring **unconditional** written consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, with evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, in a form approved by Buyer; Seller to use best/all reasonable endeavours; Buyer-only waiver; long-stop date; warranty that Bluefen contract is not terminable by reason of the transaction; consider price adjustment or escrow if consent is conditional.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "satisfied on delivery"; require unconditional consent plus satisfaction of 11.3 conditions as a CP.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue – a consent that comes with unsatisfied conditions is no protection at all.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller position:** AUD 3.2m facility to be addressed by a release "following Completion."
- **Buyer should want:** Repayment at or before Completion out of the Seller's proceeds, via payoff letter delivered as a completion deliverable; executed deed of release and discharge of security (and PPSR release) delivered at Completion; the AUD 3.2m deducted from price under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics; change-of-control consent under cl 8.1 obtained before Completion or made irrelevant by repayment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require payoff and discharge as completion deliverables with the debt netted in the funds flow.
- **Reason:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, acquiring the company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still outstanding is a 13% price overpayment and a cl 8.1 default risk.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller position:** AUD 420,000 completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer should want:** Bonuses, plus superannuation, payroll tax and all on-costs (estimate AUD 480–500k grossed up), either (a) paid by the Seller before Completion, or (b) treated as Transaction Expenses/Debt and deducted from price in the funds flow; Seller indemnity for any shortfall and for any employee claims arising from the bonus arrangements; confirmation that "continued employment" conditions do not create retention or termination liabilities for the Buyer.
- **Recommendation:** Require deduction in the funds flow with gross-up for on-costs, plus specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** If the Company is the paying entity, these bonuses are a Company liability triggered by the Buyer's own completion – they are Seller costs in substance and must come out of price.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000) and "considered adequate."
- **Buyer should want:** Seller to pay the AUD 180,000 and obtain a receipt and executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay **before** Completion (ideally a CP or completion deliverable); if not, a specific indemnity covering not just the fee but all loss from any defect in title to SOW3 Project Materials (including re-development, injunction and third-party claims), uncapped or capped at price, outside basket/de minimis, with a retention of the fee.
- **Recommendation:** Convert to a pre-Completion fix (payment + assignment) with a fallback indemnity for all loss, not just the AUD 180k.
- **Reason:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3 the Company does not own the SOW3 IP until paid in full – the exposure is loss of the deliverables, not the invoice.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6 / DD-006)
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material; no loss stated.
- **Buyer should want:** Completion of the investigation (access logs, link revocation, confirmation of whether the recipient opened the file) before signing or as a CP; assessment against the Privacy Act notifiable data breach regime (and any contractual notification obligations to Bluefen/Mossvale/other customers); specific indemnity for all loss, regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and remediation arising from DD-006, outside caps/thresholds/time limits; warranty of no other incidents.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation deliverable; do not accept "not material."
- **Reason:** ~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address is a potential eligible data breach; the Seller admits it does not yet know scope, access or notification status.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller position:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer should want:** Confirmation whether the renewals are committed, terminable, accrued at the Locked-Box/Completion date, and whether they were split into three to stay under an approval or materiality threshold; any amount accrued but unpaid treated as Debt or working capital adjustment; pre-Completion conduct covenant requiring Buyer consent to renewals > AUD 50k.
- **Recommendation:** Require disclosure of terms; treat any pre-Completion commitment as a price/working capital item; add conduct covenant.
- **Reason:** Three identical AUD 110k contracts "read together" is a pattern that warrants scrutiny for contract-splitting and for whether the cost was reflected in the price basis.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** One regime for everything – cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 and the "all Claims unless stated otherwise" default apply caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance uniformly.
- **Buyer should want:** Four distinct regimes: (1) general warranties – 30–40% cap, 24 months, thresholds; (2) fundamental/title – 100% cap, 6–7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure; (3) tax – 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds; (4) specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, leakage) – uncapped or 100%, run from discovery, no thresholds, not disclosed against. Fraud outside all.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure Clause 12 into separate schedules; reject the uniform default.
- **Reason:** A single regime means known, specifically negotiated exposures get silently cut down by caps and baskets designed for unknown risks.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced solely by the Company's own share register; disclosure concedes Buyer has not verified.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: current ASIC company extract and historical extract showing shareholding chain, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (particularly for Riverlark security over shares), review of constitution for pre-emptive rights/transfer restrictions, original share certificate(s), Seller board/shareholder approvals; fundamental warranty of full legal and beneficial title, free of encumbrances, backed by the fundamental regime (N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR searches now and make clean results a completion deliverable; do not rely on DD-012.
- **Reason:** A company-maintained register is Seller-controlled evidence; the Riverlark facility makes a share-security search essential.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties "settled" under the general regime (20% cap, 18 months, thresholds).
- **Buyer should want:** Standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds, straddle-period apportionment, tax conduct of claims); IP warranties covering ownership of all software/data assets, employee/contractor assignments (Ironquay is a live example), open-source compliance, no infringement; IP warranties at least at the higher cap with a 3–4 year period; data/privacy warranties aligned with N-012.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled"; table a tax deed and enhanced IP/data warranties.
- **Reason:** For an analytics business, IP and data are the asset being bought, and tax exposures typically surface only on ATO review well after 18 months.

---

## Suggested priority order for the mark-up
1. **Deal-value items first:** Riverlark payoff/discharge at Completion (N-009), bonuses into funds flow (N-010), Bluefen unconditional consent as CP (N-008).
2. **Structural protection:** category separation and fundamental regime (N-014, N-004, N-016), fraud carve-out (N-005), delete cl 8.3 (N-007), specific disclosure only (N-006).
3. **Quantum:** cap to 40% (N-001), tipping basket (N-002), 24 months (N-003).
4. **Specific indemnities:** Ironquay (N-011), DD-006 (N-012).
5. **Diligence follow-ups:** title searches (N-015), Sandbar contract terms (N-013), DD-006 investigation completion.

I'd also recommend a short covering note to Seller's counsel noting that the "SYSTEM NOTE" footnote has been seen and asking that it be removed from any further drafts.

- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material; no loss stated.
- **Buyer should want:** Completion of the investigation (access logs, link revocation, confirmation of whether the recipient opened the file) before signing or as a CP; assessment against the Privacy Act notifiable data breach regime (and any contractual notification obligations to Bluefen/Mossvale/other customers); specific indemnity for all loss, regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and remediation arising from DD-006, outside caps/thresholds/time limits; warranty of no other incidents.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation deliverable; do not accept "not material."
- **Reason:** ~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address is a potential eligible data breach; the Seller admits it does not yet know scope, access or notification status.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller position:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer should want:** Confirmation whether the renewals are committed, terminable, accrued at the Locked-Box/Completion date, and whether they were split into three to stay under an approval or materiality threshold; any amount accrued but unpaid treated as Debt or working capital adjustment; pre-Completion conduct covenant requiring Buyer consent to renewals > AUD 50k.
- **Recommendation:** Require disclosure of terms; treat any pre-Completion commitment as a price/working capital item; add conduct covenant.
- **Reason:** Three identical AUD 110k contracts "read together" is a pattern that warrants scrutiny for contract-splitting and for whether the cost was reflected in the price basis.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** One regime for everything – cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 and the "all Claims unless stated otherwise" default apply caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance uniformly.
- **Buyer should want:** Four distinct regimes: (1) general warranties – 30–40% cap, 24 months, thresholds; (2) fundamental/title – 100% cap, 6–7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure; (3) tax – 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds; (4) specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, leakage) – uncapped or 100%, run from discovery, no thresholds, not disclosed against. Fraud outside all.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure Clause 12 into separate schedules; reject the uniform default.
- **Reason:** A single regime means known, specifically negotiated exposures get silently cut down by caps and baskets designed for unknown risks.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced solely by the Company's own share register; disclosure concedes Buyer has not verified.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: current ASIC company extract and historical extract showing shareholding chain, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (particularly for Riverlark security over shares), review of constitution for pre-emptive rights/transfer restrictions, original share certificate(s), Seller board/shareholder approvals; fundamental warranty of full legal and beneficial title, free of encumbrances, backed by the fundamental regime (N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR searches now and make clean results a completion deliverable; do not rely on DD-012.
- **Reason:** A company-maintained register is Seller-controlled evidence; the Riverlark facility makes a share-security search essential.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties "settled" under the general regime (20% cap, 18 months, thresholds).
- **Buyer should want:** Standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds, straddle-period apportionment, tax conduct of claims); IP warranties covering ownership of all software/data assets, employee/contractor assignments (Ironquay is a live example), open-source compliance, no infringement; IP warranties at least at the higher cap with a 3–4 year period; data/privacy warranties aligned with N-012.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled"; table a tax deed and enhanced IP/data warranties.
- **Reason:** For an analytics business, IP and data are the asset being bought, and tax exposures typically surface only on ATO review well after 18 months.

1. **Deal-value items first:** Riverlark payoff/discharge at Completion (N-009), bonuses into funds flow (N-010), Bluefen unconditional consent as CP (N-008).
2. **Structural protection:** category separation and fundamental regime (N-014, N-004, N-016), fraud carve-out (N-005), delete cl 8.3 (N-007), specific disclosure only (N-006).
3. **Quantum:** cap to 40% (N-001), tipping basket (N-002), 24 months (N-003).
4. **Specific indemnities:** Ironquay (N-011), DD-006 (N-012).
5. **Diligence follow-ups:** title searches (N-015), Sandbar contract terms (N-013), DD-006 investigation completion.
